chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:

On the Day of Resurrection, two believing servants will be brought to stand for the reckoning. Both are from the people of Paradise, one was poor in this world and the other was rich in this world. So the poor one will say: "O Lord! For what reason was I made to stand? By Your glory, You surely know that You did not give me authority so that I could be just or unjust in it, nor did You grant me wealth so that I could fulfill what is due from it or withhold it, and my sustenance only came to me in bare sufficiency, according to what You knew and decreed for me." So God — Glorified be His Majesty — will say: "My servant has spoken the truth; release him, let him enter Paradise." The other will remain until the sweat flows from him so much that if forty camels were to drink from it, it would suffice them. Then he will enter Paradise.

The poor one will say to him: "What kept you?" He will say: "The length of the reckoning. One matter kept coming to me after another, being forgiven of me, then I was asked about another matter, until God — Mighty and Majestic — encompassed me in His mercy and joined me with the repentant ones. So who are you?" He will say: "I am the poor one who was with you a little while ago." He (the rich one) will say: "Bliss has indeed changed you after my (leaving you)."

key_terms.التَّائِبُون: The repentant ones — those who turned back to God in repentance; here they receive divine mercy
key_terms.النَّعِيم: Bliss, felicity — the transformative pleasure of Paradise
key_terms.الْحِسَاب: The reckoning/accounting — the divine judgment of a person's earthly deeds on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.الْكَفَاف: Bare sufficiency — having just enough to subsist, neither affluence nor destitution
key_terms.الْوِلَايَة: Authority, governance — a position of leadership or power entrusted by God, which carries moral accountability

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the reckoning of the poor versus the rich on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates a vivid eschatological scene in which two believers — one formerly poor and one formerly wealthy — both destined for Paradise, stand before God on the Day of Resurrection. The poor man enters immediately because he had no authority to misuse nor wealth to mismanage; God validates his plea and dismisses him at once. The rich man, by contrast, endures an exhausting, protracted reckoning — symbolized by a flood of sweat sufficient to water forty camels — as each of his worldly responsibilities and actions is examined and forgiven one by one. This hadith teaches that the wealth and power entrusted to a person in this world carries an enormous accounting burden, whereas the pious poor are spared this ordeal. It also illustrates the transformation wrought by Paradise, which so changes the formerly impoverished servant that even his old companion fails to recognize him.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa`id from `Ali b. al-Hakam from Dawud b. al-Nu`man from Ishaq b. `Ammar from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:

On the Day of Resurrection, two believing servants will be brought for judgment. Both are from the people of Paradise, but one was poor in this world, and the other was rich in this world. So, the poor one will say: “O Lord! Why was I brought? By Your glory, You surely know that You did not give me authority with which I could have been just or unjust, nor did you grant me wealth with which I could have given rightly or withheld it. My sustenance was not but enough to subsist poorly.” So, Allah will say: “You have spoken the truth, My servant, let him go enter Paradise.” So, the other will remain [for long], and he will sweat so much [over that time] that if forty camels would drink from it, it would suffice them. Then, he will enter Paradise.

So, the poor one will say to him: “What kept you?” So, he said: “The length of the judgment. One thing came up after another, which were forgiven of me. Then, I would be asked about another thing until Allah would encompass me in His mercy. He made me join the repentant. So, who are you?” So, he will say: “I am the poor one who was with you earlier.” So, he will say: “Bliss has changed you.”
